question: What does "LBW" stand for in cricket?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Leg Before Wicket**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Leg Before Wicket (LBW) is one of the ways a batsman can be dismissed in the sport of cricket.
 
• The rule is designed to prevent the batsman from using their legs to block the ball from hitting the stumps.
 
• The umpire decides if the batsman is out LBW based on specific criteria defined in the cricket laws.
 
• The LBW decision involves the ball pitching in line with the stumps, not pitching outside the leg stump, and the ball hitting any part of the batsman's body before hitting the bat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Last Ball Wicket:**

 
 
• This term does not exist in official cricket terminology.
 
• It may refer to a wicket taken on the last ball of an over or the innings, but it is not an official term.
 
 
 
• **Leg Before Wicket (LBW):**
 
 
• This is a legitimate method of dismissing a batsman in cricket.
 
• For a batsman to be given out LBW, the ball must either be pitching in line with the stumps or outside off-stump, and it must impact the batsman in line with the stumps.
 
• The ball must also be predicted to hit the stumps if it had not hit the batsman's leg.
 
 
 
• **Long Boundary Wicket:**
 
 
• This term is not recognized in cricket terminology.
 
• It may be a misinterpretation or a colloquial term but has no official standing in cricket rules.
 
 
 
• **Leg Break Wrist:**
 
 
• This term could refer to the type of delivery bowled by a leg-spin bowler.
 
• Leg break refers to the ball spinning from the leg side to the off side for a right-handed batsman.
 
• However, it does not pertain to the method of dismissal.
